title: M3.2.5 Factory Reliability and Scale Readiness
purpose: Add an executable reliability layer around the promoted M3.2 AI Kit Factory: storage-independent resource identity, deterministic FactoryRun/evidence records, self-verification, and a benchmark gate that proves both PASS and justified HOLD behavior.
invariants: Promoted M3.2 factory_gate.py remains byte-unchanged and authoritative for canonical, pedagogical, semantic and binding decisions.
Logical resource identity is resourceId + version + sha256; physical host paths are never emitted in FactoryRun or evidence records.
Resource version participates in M3.2.5 run identity but does not weaken or replace M3.2 byte-level semantic-review binding.
FactoryRun and evidence bundle are deterministic manifests, not storage containers and not learner-kit fields.
Benchmark PASS requires both successful qualifications and justified HOLD qualifications.
Git stores code, contracts, tests and benchmark policy, not a large source/kit/media corpus.
No source extraction, OCR, model API, backend, runtime AI, publishing or learner-runtime mutation is introduced.
M3.3, M3.4, Gate3, Gate4 and M4+ remain HOLD.
requiredEvidence: Exact seven-path delta from promoted M3.2 main.
Repository governance PASS and PR scope PASS.
Existing M3.2 product oracle remains PASS with factory_gate.py byte-identical to baseline.
Moving identical resource bytes to a different host path leaves emitted resource identity, evidence bundle and FactoryRun byte-identical.
Changing only a resource version changes resourceSetDigest and runId while preserving the M3.2 byte-level context digest.
FactoryRun self-verification rejects tampered decision, resource, artifact, validator, bundle or run digests.
Source byte drift still produces M3.2 review-binding HOLD.
Semantic HOLD is preserved with non-empty reasons.
Benchmark contract covers mathematics, physics, computer science, history, law, medicine, literature and management.
Benchmark requires at least eight distinct runs, at least two PASS, at least two HOLD and no more than 25 percent human escalation.
Benchmark cases must use distinct source-content digests; changing only resource IDs or versions cannot make one source count as multiple domains.
Duplicate FactoryRun identity cannot count twice.
Dedicated exact-head CI produces reproducible evidence.
adversarialTests: Same resource bytes at different physical paths.
Same resource bytes with different logical version.
One-byte resource drift after semantic review.
Tampered nested factory evidence or evidence-bundle digest.
Benchmark relabels identical source bytes under a new resource version and different domain.
Any host path leaked into emitted FactoryRun evidence.
independentReview: The reliability layer composes around the promoted M3.2 gate instead of modifying it.
Exact-head CI re-runs the promoted M3.2 oracle before the new reliability oracle.
A later real-source benchmark must contain both independent PASS and independent justified HOLD cases before M3.2.5 promotion.
No human gate is required for this implementation unless real benchmark execution exposes an unresolved semantic/product ambiguity.
rollback: Remove the additive M3.2.5 reliability module, benchmark contract, tests/workflow/router entry and restore the factory README. Promoted M3.2 factory_gate.py, learner runtime, canonical contracts and stored data remain unchanged.
